1.why: All ten screens show a static, uncluttered card layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs anywhere.

2.why: Primary actions are bold blue buttons and headings are prominent, but the consent checkbox on step 8 is separated from its label with broken wrapping, so not every important item stands out.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task (email, code, password, consent) with one obvious field and button, making the needed element quick to locate.

4.why: The flow spans at least seven steps and imposes five password rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol) plus transcription of a 40-character token, so the user must remember many rules and steps.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager prompt, or explicit autofill option appears on the sign-in or password screens.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — the recovery token is a long random string shown only in the Logs panel and the code field starts empty.

7.why: Body text is one to two short plain sentences per screen (e.g., 'Enter your account email address'), which is short and readable.

8.why: No error message is displayed in any of the ten screenshots, so whether errors explain the problem and fix cannot be confirmed.

9.why: No concrete examples are shown — no sample email, no example password format, and no placeholder text inside the empty input fields.

10.why: There are no alternative authentication choices such as code or face login; the only offered path is email plus password with recovery codes.

11.why: Every screen offers only one primary action and at most one secondary link, so the user never faces many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Dedicated confirmation screens state outcomes ('Password updated', 'Privacy conditions accepted'), though step 1 deliberately gives an ambiguous result about account eligibility.

13.why: Each new step carries a brief instructional line and a persistent 'Keep your account safe' tip appears on every screen.

14.why: Recovery links such as 'Request another code' and 'Forgot password?' let the user retry after a mistake.

15.why: All ten steps reuse the identical header, card, notice bar, and Logs panel structure, so the design is highly consistent.
